case.pattern_description: Threshold structuring on a compromised card: 4 online purchases ($469.82, $467.06, $496.08, $488.63) placed within about an hour, each kept just under $500, the level at which authorisation checks tighten. It affects cardholders whose card numbers are already compromised and matches five closed cases the bank confirmed but could not map to a known typology; the agent found it by scanning the card's window for clusters of same-band amounts.

sar.narrative: Customer C01890, holder of card C01890-K1, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-11-23 18:00 and 2016-11-23 18:27, 4 transaction(s) totalling $1,921.59 were made on the card online: $469.82 (3481356, 2016-11-23 18:00), $467.06 (3481393, 2016-11-23 18:11), $496.08 (3481403, 2016-11-23 18:16), $488.63 (3481444, 2016-11-23 18:27). Every amount sat just below $500 and the purchases were placed minutes apart, a pattern consistent with deliberately staying under an authorisation threshold. The activity is suspicious because: 4 online purchases within 27 minutes, each between $400 and $500 ($469.82, $467.06, $496.08, $488.63; total $1,921.59). It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-3841, CC-3907, CC-4124. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placed linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retains the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.
